sources.title: Identifying and managing conflicts of interest in a charity
sources.author: Charity Commission for England and Wales; updated 22 April 2026
sources.sections: Definition, loyalty conflicts, governing-document check and steps 1–5 including recording disposition
sources.supported_use: Distinguish disclosure from managed and recorded participation.
sources.limits: England and Wales charity trustees; duties, quorum and authorization rules are not generalized. Linked legal analysis was not inspected. P6 is original fiction, not a legal finding.

sources.title: Preventing Policy Capture: Integrity in Public Decision Making
sources.author: OECD; 30 March 2017
sources.sections: Landing-page abstract: capture definition and four complementary safeguards
sources.supported_use: Frame dependency, participation, transparency, accountability and integrity checks.
sources.limits: Abstract only, not the full report or its case studies. Three institutional cases and pressure tests are original analytical fiction, not OECD findings about actual bodies.

sources.title: How to File a Whistleblower Complaint
sources.author: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.sections: Complaint remit, lawfully obtained supporting material, varying deadlines, anonymity limit and employer notification; separate safety-complaint link
sources.supported_use: Explain why reporting routes and protection conditions must be checked separately.
sources.limits: U.S. specified retaliation statutes, not universal worker coverage. The underlying safety complaint is distinct. No confidentiality guarantee, personal deadline, legal coverage determination or actual filing. No linked form or case investigation.

sources.title: Decision-making for charity trustees
sources.author: Charity Commission for England and Wales; updated 9 September 2024
sources.sections: Powers and governing documents; clear records; independent judgment and disagreement; delegation and reporting
sources.supported_use: Relate legitimate authority to reviewable decisions and accountable delegation.
sources.limits: England and Wales charity context, not a universal constitution. Selected sections, not linked law or Commission case decisions. R2 appointments, deadlines and appeal powers are original fiction.

sources.title: Promising Practices for Preventing Harassment
sources.author: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission; 21 November 2017
sources.sections: Leadership/accountability and complaint-system passages on independent routes, impartial investigation, privacy, retaliation and corrective action
sources.supported_use: Separate protection, fair determination, communication and institutional follow-through.
sources.limits: Historical nonbinding technical assistance, not current legal guidance for every jurisdiction. No force of law; linked report and statutory footnotes are not adopted. Financial-report case and A7 are original. No actual investigation or finding.

sources.title: Creating a cash flow budget
sources.author: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; Your Money, Your Goals tool, November 2018
sources.sections: Four-page PDF text: beginning balance, income, outflow including savings and carried ending balance; negative periods
sources.supported_use: Teach cash-flow reconciliation and the importance of dated availability.
sources.limits: Educational worksheet only; figures and layout were not used. No full toolkit, benefits eligibility rule or personal budget recommendation. Daily calendars and figures are original.

sources.title: An essential guide to building an emergency fund
sources.author: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; page modified 29 October 2025
sources.sections: What a fund is, situation-specific amounts, saving approaches, accessible storage and use/replenishment
sources.supported_use: Connect a reserve to a disruption, capacity and access.
sources.limits: General educational framing, not a universal target, verified product, account opening or personal benefits advice. Linked toolkit and quiz not inspected. D4 is a supplied fictional disclosure.

sources.title: Is the money I keep in my payment app safe?
sources.author: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; reviewed 1 June 2023
sources.sections: Explanation of differing payment-app protection and service conditions
sources.supported_use: Require verification of protection rather than inferring it from an app label.
sources.limits: U.S. educational explanation; no provider or product has been verified, and no guarantee of continuous access is inferred. FDIC pages failed retrieval and are not credited as inspected.

sources.title: What is the difference between a loan interest rate and the APR?
sources.author: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; reviewed 28 August 2026
sources.sections: Interest-rate versus broader APR explanation and fee comparison
sources.supported_use: Keep the stated nominal simple-interest examples separate from APR.
sources.limits: U.S. auto-loan context only; no universal disclosure rule or regulatory APR calculation is applied. Fictional end-payment loans are not current offers or personal borrowing advice.

sources.title: Beginners’ Guide to Asset Allocation, Diversification, and Rebalancing
sources.author: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Investor.gov
sources.sections: Horizon and risk tolerance; diversification within/between categories; broad fund versus sector focus; changing circumstances
sources.supported_use: Inspect concentration and connect risk and access to the money’s purpose.
sources.limits: Educational examples only. Historical return claims, stock-count rules, allocation percentages and product recommendations are not adopted. No real prospectus inspected. Original P/Q cards expose identical holdings.

sources.title: How Fees and Expenses Affect Your Investment Portfolio – Investor Bulletin
sources.author: SEC Office of Investor Education and Assistance; 23 July 2025
sources.sections: Fee effect, disclosure sources, transaction and ongoing fees, account/product questions
sources.supported_use: Explain retained growth and inspect explicit versus missing cost fields.
sources.limits: Staff educational bulletin, not a rule. No actual account terms, adviser agreement, linked enforcement case or underlying fund disclosure inspected. Toy net-growth paths are not forecasts and are independent of P/Q fees.

sources.title: I would like to be able to have my friend or family member help with my bill-paying and banking. What are my options?
sources.author: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; modified 18 March 2024
sources.sections: Trusted contact distinction and financial-help role options including powers
sources.supported_use: Answer narrowly that a trusted contact does not automatically obtain bill-paying authority.
sources.limits: No specific document, capacity, appointment, provider acceptance or local validity is determined. No legal drafting, signature, credentials, inquiry transmission or transaction.

sources.title: What to Know About Life Insurance Beneficiaries
sources.author: National Association of Insurance Commissioners; 12 September 2023
sources.sections: Policyholder and beneficiary information, insurer and policy location, review after life changes
sources.supported_use: Make appropriate policy-location information findable and beneficiary questions explicit.
sources.limits: U.S. educational guidance, not policy suitability, current designation or estate validity. No policy locator search or linked resource used. A life policy does not establish coverage for living absence.

sources.title: Online Shopping
sources.author: U.S. Federal Trade Commission; May 2023
sources.sections: Comparison shopping, complete cost, condition and return-policy questions
sources.supported_use: Compare a complete price and unresolved burdens rather than a sticker price alone.
sources.limits: No seller, market quote or product was inspected. Shipping/dispute legal deadlines and payment-method advice are not imported into the exercise. All chair prices and observations are fictional.

sources.title: Tax withholding
sources.author: Internal Revenue Service
sources.sections: Pay-as-you-go introduction, withholding definition and under/over-withholding explanation
sources.supported_use: Distinguish withholding from final tax liability.
sources.limits: U.S. federal concept only, not a tax computation, withholding recommendation or filing determination. Estimator, forms, tax tables and linked publications were not used.
